Numeric == / != carries a known SIGNED scale or unknown plus an independent multiplicative-constant capability: when known scales differ, only a capable SMALLER-scale side may be padded; an unknown scale rejects. ORDERING (< <= > >=) is exempt. TWO contexts trigger this code: (1) a COMPUTED FIELD whose declared scale is incompatible with its expression (e.g. a field re-scaled to 2 places while the Sum-computed field stays scale 0) — re-scale the computed field or explicitly round the expression, doing both edits in ONE `apply` so the terminal gate sees a consistent model; expect a SECOND rejection to surface if the operation also reads its own computed field, because this scale comparison is decided ahead of that refusal; (2) numeric == / != with incompatible derived scales — round one side to a known compatible scale, or accept it with allowDifferingDecimals:true on the rule spec (the kernel's one suppressible warning — it prepends @SuppressWarning(MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_DEC_PLACES)).
diagnostics.explain: MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_DEC_PLACES ("the fractional digits of lhs and rhs are different") fires when numeric == / != cannot reconcile the operands' derived signed-scale/capability summaries, OR when a computed field is incompatible with its expression. It is not specific to any one operator (Sum, Equal, …); the scale-coupling is the constraint, so the corrective is context-dependent.

So this code does NOT imply the target is a date field. If the target really is textual, the fix is to stop the literal looking like a date, not to change the field.
diagnostics.explain: Which class a wrong-kind constant assignment reports is an ordered ladder over the (constant, target) PAIR, not a function of the target: a BOOLEAN target reports MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_YESNO and a CONFIRM target MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_YES for any constant at all; failing those, a temporal constant reports THIS code at every remaining target; only then does the target's own kind decide. Measured in KERNEL-FINDINGS entry KF257, which carries the ladder and its controls.
